**Jorge Luis Sampaoli Moya** (Spanish pronunciation: [[ˈxoɾxe
sampaˈoli]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"); born 13 March 1960) is
an Argentine [football coach](/wiki/Head_coach "Head coach") who is the head
coach of [Campeonato Brasileiro Série
A](/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_S%C3%A9rie_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série A")
club [Atlético Mineiro](/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Mineiro "Clube Atlético
Mineiro"). Sampaoli started out as a youth player and eventually switched to
management after a severe injury.[1]

Sampaoli started with an impressive coaching run at [Coronel
Bolognesi](/wiki/Coronel_Bolognesi "Coronel Bolognesi") of Peru in 2004, and
continued with brief but successful terms at
[O'Higgins](/wiki/O%27Higgins_F.C. "O'Higgins F.C.") of Chile and
[Emelec](/wiki/CS_Emelec "CS Emelec") of Ecuador.

Sampaoli earned praise as the head coach of [Universidad de
Chile](/wiki/Club_Universidad_de_Chile "Club Universidad de Chile"), winning
three league titles and the [Copa Sudamericana](/wiki/2011_Copa_Sudamericana
"2011 Copa Sudamericana") championship. This success led him to coach the
[Chilean men's national team](/wiki/Chile_national_football_team "Chile
national football team") in 2012, replacing [Claudio
Borghi](/wiki/Claudio_Borghi_\(football_manager\) "Claudio Borghi \(football
manager\)"). He led the Chile national football team to their first [Copa
América](/wiki/Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "Copa América") title, after defeating
[Argentina](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national
football team") in the [final](/wiki/2015_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica_Final "2015 Copa
América Final") in the [2015 tournament](/wiki/2015_Copa_America "2015 Copa
America") in Chile. He is well known for his attacking tactics which are
similar to those of [Marcelo Bielsa](/wiki/Marcelo_Bielsa "Marcelo Bielsa"),
according to the press and fans alike.[2]

On 28 June 2016, Sampaoli signed a two-year contract with
[Sevilla](/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC").[3] After spending only one year in
Spain and leading Sevilla to fourth spot in La Liga, and ensuring [Champions
League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") football [the
following season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA
Champions League"), Sampaoli left the club to coach the [Argentina national
team](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football
team"),[4] where he left by mutual consent, after a disappointing run in the
[2018 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"). He
eventually agreed to coach Brazilian club [Santos](/wiki/Santos_FC "Santos
FC") in 2019, staying one year and leading the club to the second position in
the league. In March 2021, he returned to manage in European football when he
was appointed at French side [Marseille](/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille
"Olympique de Marseille"). In October 2022, he returned to manage
[Sevilla](/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC"). On 21 March 2023, he was sacked by
[Sevilla](/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") and replaced by [José Luis
Mendilibar](/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Luis_Mendilibar "José Luis Mendilibar"). He
returned to French football and was appointed manager of Rennes in November
2024 but was sacked in January 2025.

## Early life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section:
Early life")]

Jorge Sampaoli was born in [Casilda](/wiki/Casilda "Casilda"), in the [Caseros
Department](/wiki/Caseros_Department "Caseros Department") of [Santa Fe
Province](/wiki/Santa_Fe_Province "Santa Fe Province"), Argentina. In his
youth he played for amateur sides in his local league before joining the
[Newell's Old Boys](/wiki/Newell%27s_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys") youth
setup, where he later said he suffered from stage fright that prevented him
from progressing. [5] While at the club he suffered fractures to his tibia and
fibula in 1979, forcing him to retire from playing at age 19.[1] During his
final playing years and early coaching career he worked part-time at a
bank.[6]

## Coaching career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section:
Coaching career")]

### Early career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section:
Early career")]

In October 1991, aged just 31, Sampaoli acted as an interim coach for hometown
side Club Atlético Alumni, as manager Mario Bonavera was out on a personal
trip. During that season, he was already working as a fitness coach aside from
being a [defensive midfielder](/wiki/Midfielder#Defensive_midfielder
"Midfielder").[6] He was given the role of manager of the club's youth setup
in the following year, but only retired in 1993.[6] In 1994 he was named
manager of the first team, taking the club to the finals of the Liga
Casildense de Fútbol, but lost it to CA 9 de Julio de Arequito.[6] In the
following season, he again reached the finals, but suffered defeat to the very
same club.[7]

For the 1996 season, Sampaoli was appointed at 9 Julio's rivals CA Belgrano de
Arequito, and coached to win the year's league title with the side.[8] In May
of that year,[6] he was hired by [Primera B
Metropolitana](/wiki/Primera_B_Metropolitana "Primera B Metropolitana") side
[Argentino de Rosario](/wiki/Argentino_de_Rosario "Argentino de Rosario"),[9]
and ended the season in the 13th position. He subsequently returned to Alumni
and Belgrano,[8] before taking over CA Aprendices Casildenses in 1999; with
the latter side, he won two consecutive Liga Casildense titles.[6]

Sampaoli returned to a third stint with Alumni in 2001,[6] after a short stint
back at Argentino de Rosario in the previous year.[10] Despite reaching the
finals of the Liga Casildense, he lost it to former side Aprendices.[6]

### Juan Aurich

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section:
Juan Aurich")]

On 9 January 2002, Sampaoli was appointed coach of [Peruvian Primera
División](/wiki/Peruvian_Primera_Divisi%C3%B3n "Peruvian Primera División")
side [Juan Aurich](/wiki/Juan_Aurich "Juan Aurich"); it was the first
professional club in his career.[11][12] On 24 February, he directed his first
professional game against [Universitario](/wiki/Universitario_de_Deportes
"Universitario de Deportes"), where they lost 2–1 after leading the whole game
due to a [penalty](/wiki/Penalty_kick_\(association_football\) "Penalty kick
\(association football\)") scored by [Carlos
Flores](/wiki/Carlos_Flores_\(footballer,_born_1974\) "Carlos Flores
\(footballer, born 1974\)") (66th minute).[13]

Sampaoli had a poor spell in Juan Aurich, directing only eight games, five of
which the team lost and two where the team tied with [Coopsol
Trujillo](/wiki/Coopsol_Trujillo "Coopsol Trujillo") and [Alianza
Lima](/wiki/Alianza_Lima "Alianza Lima"). The team only won against
[Cienciano](/wiki/Cienciano "Cienciano") 2–0 with goals from César Sánchez and
Flores. He left the club in April, when Aurich was sitting at the bottom of
the table.[14]

### Sport Boys

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section:
Sport Boys")]

Months later, in June, Sampaoli was hired by [Sport Boys](/wiki/Sport_Boys
"Sport Boys") to direct the team in the [Torneo
Descentralizado](/wiki/Torneo_Descentralizado "Torneo Descentralizado"),
debuting with a 3–1 loss to Coopsol.[15] His side finished sixth in the
tournament, achieving important triumphs over Alianza (1–0 with a goal of
[Alfredo Carmona](/wiki/Alfredo_Carmona "Alfredo Carmona")) and Universitario
(2–0 with goals by [Paolo de la Haza](/wiki/Paolo_de_la_Haza "Paolo de la
Haza") and Carmona again at [Estadio
Monumental](/wiki/Estadio_Monumental_%22U%22 "Estadio Monumental "U"")). He
left the club during the [2003 Torneo
Descentralizado](/wiki/2003_Torneo_Descentralizado "2003 Torneo
Descentralizado"), after a player's strike.[16]

### Coronel Bolognesi

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section:
Coronel Bolognesi")]

In 2004, Sampaoli was named coach of fellow top-tier side [Coronel
Bolognesi](/wiki/Coronel_Bolognesi "Coronel Bolognesi"),[16] replacing
[Roberto Mosquera](/wiki/Roberto_Mosquera "Roberto Mosquera").[17] There, he
had an irregular start, but soon coached to settle the team during the
Peruvian 2005's [Descentralizado](/wiki/2005_Torneo_Descentralizado "2005
Torneo Descentralizado"), finishing fifth in the Apertura, and then coached to
finish third in that same year's Clausura, taking the club to their first
international competition.

Sampaoli opted to leave the club in December 2005, but returned on 27 June
2006, replacing compatriot Raúl Donsanti.[18] Competing in the 2006's
[Clausura](/wiki/2006_Torneo_Descentralizado "2006 Torneo Descentralizado") as
well as in the Sudamericana tournament, his side finished third in the
national league.[16]

### Sporting Cristal

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section:
Sporting Cristal")]

In 2007, Sampaoli was hired as the head coach of [Sporting
Cristal](/wiki/Sporting_Cristal "Sporting Cristal"). However, his time at
Cristal turned out to be disappointing after 18 matches and only five wins. He
was dismissed from the "Celestes" in May of that year, ending his Peruvian
coaching career.[16]

### O'Higgins

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section:
O'Higgins")]

On 12 December 2007, Sampaoli arrived in [Chile](/wiki/Chile "Chile") to take
over at [O'Higgins](/wiki/O%27Higgins_F.C. "O'Higgins F.C."), in the place of
[Jorge Garcés](/wiki/Jorge_Garc%C3%A9s "Jorge Garcés").[19] In 2008, the team
proved to be tough to crack for bigger Chilean teams, finishing third in that
year's [Apertura](/wiki/2008_Chilean_Primera_Divisi%C3%B3n_season "2008
Chilean Primera División season"). They were eliminated by powerhouse
[Universidad de Chile](/wiki/Club_Universidad_de_Chile "Club Universidad de
Chile") in the playoff quarterfinals.[_[citation
needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The next year turned out to be a tough year for Sampaoli, as "La Celeste" had
an irregular campaign, where they finished in 8th place, and, despite
qualifying to the [2009's Apertura
Playoffs](/wiki/2009_Chilean_Primera_Division_season "2009 Chilean Primera
Division season"), ended up being thrashed 6–1 in the second leg of the
quarterfinals by [Unión Española](/wiki/Uni%C3%B3n_Espa%C3%B1ola "Unión
Española"). He resigned in August 2009, being replaced by Geraldo Silva. [20]

### Emelec

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section:
Emelec")]

On 18 December 2009, Sampaoli was named [Emelec](/wiki/C.S._Emelec "C.S.
Emelec") coach for the upcoming season.[21] Under his guidance, the team
competed in the [2010 Copa Libertadores](/wiki/2010_Copa_Libertadores "2010
Copa Libertadores"), being eliminated in the group stage, but had an
impressive run in the local competition, finishing first in the [2010
tournament first
stage](/wiki/2010_Campeonato_Ecuatoriano_de_F%C3%BAtbol_Serie_A "2010
Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A"), earning them a spot in the [2010
Copa Sudamericana](/wiki/2010_Copa_Sudamericana "2010 Copa Sudamericana") and
[2011 Copa Libertadores](/wiki/2011_Copa_Libertadores "2011 Copa
Libertadores") preliminary stage.[22]

That year, Emelec faced [Liga de
Quito](/wiki/Liga_Deportiva_Universitaria_de_Quito "Liga Deportiva
Universitaria de Quito"), who finished in first place in that year's [second
half](/wiki/2010_Campeonato_Ecuatoriano_de_Futbol_Serie_A "2010 Campeonato
Ecuatoriano de Futbol Serie A"),[23] but ended up losing.[24]

### Universidad de Chile

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=10 "Edit
section: Universidad de Chile")]

On 15 December 2010, Sampaoli was presented as coach of [Universidad de
Chile](/wiki/Club_Universidad_de_Chile "Club Universidad de Chile").[25] With
the side he achieved impressive results, winning the [2011
Apertura](/wiki/2011_Torneo_Apertura_\(Chile\) "2011 Torneo Apertura
\(Chile\)"), the [2011 Clausura](/wiki/2011_Torneo_Clausura_\(Chile\) "2011
Torneo Clausura \(Chile\)"), the [2012
Apertura](/wiki/2012_Torneo_Apertura_\(Chile\) "2012 Torneo Apertura
\(Chile\)") and the [2011 Copa Sudamericana](/wiki/2011_Copa_Sudamericana
"2011 Copa Sudamericana").[26] He left the club after accepting an offer from
the national team, with 80 wins in 135 matches.[27]

### Chile national team

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=11 "Edit
section: Chile national team")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Jorge_Sampaoli_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-
Jorge_Sampaoli_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Jorge_Sampaoli_\(cropped\).jpg)Sampaoli
coaching the [Chile national team](/wiki/Chile_national_football_team "Chile
national football team") in 2013

On 3 December 2012, Chile's [Asociación Nacional de Fútbol
Profesional](/wiki/Asociaci%C3%B3n_Nacional_de_F%C3%BAtbol_Profesional
"Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional") announced that Sampaoli would
take over as coach of the [national team](/wiki/Chile_national_football_team
"Chile national football team") after a successful run with _La U_.[28][29]
His arrival brought about a turnaround in performances and results, with Chile
winning three of their first four World Cup qualifiers after his appointment.
Under Sampaoli, Chile returned to the energetic, high-pressing game of
[Marcelo Bielsa](/wiki/Marcelo_Bielsa "Marcelo Bielsa"),[30] the Argentinian
coach who inspired Sampaoli's coaching philosophy.

In 2015, Sampaoli led Chile to victory in the [2015 Copa
America](/wiki/2015_Copa_Am%C3%A9rica "2015 Copa América"), the country's
first major trophy.[31] On 30 November of that year, he was named on the final
three-man shortlist for the 2015 [FIFA World Coach of the
Year](/wiki/FIFA_World_Coach_of_the_Year "FIFA World Coach of the Year")
award, joined by Spaniards [Pep Guardiola](/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep
Guardiola") ([Bayern Munich](/wiki/Bayern_Munich "Bayern Munich")) and [Luis
Enrique](/wiki/Luis_Enrique_\(footballer\) "Luis Enrique \(footballer\)")
([Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona")).[32][33]

On 19 January 2016, Sampaoli resigned as coach of Chile, after allegedly
having disputes with [Arturo Salah](/wiki/Arturo_Salah "Arturo Salah"),
recently elected president of ANFP.[34]

### Sevilla

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=12 "Edit
section: Sevilla")]

On 27 June 2016, [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") club
[Sevilla](/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") announced that Sampaoli would take
over Sevilla on a two-year deal.[3] On 15 January 2017, his side beat
[Zinedine Zidane](/wiki/Zinedine_Zidane "Zinedine Zidane")'s [Real
Madrid](/wiki/Real_Madrid_C.F. "Real Madrid C.F.") 2–1, ending their 40-match
unbeaten run.[35]

### Argentina national team

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=13 "Edit
section: Argentina national team")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/ECUADOR_VS_ARGENTINA_%2837627106871%29.jpg/250px-
ECUADOR_VS_ARGENTINA_%2837627106871%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:ECUADOR_VS_ARGENTINA_\(37627106871\).jpg)Sampaoli
in October 2017, celebrating Argentina's qualification for the 2018 World Cup

On 20 May 2017, the [Argentine Football
Association](/wiki/Argentine_Football_Association "Argentine Football
Association") announced that Sampaoli would take over as the new coach of [the
national team](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national
football team"). He was officially presented on 1 June 2017. Sampaoli's first
game in charge was a friendly match against
[Brazil](/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team")
on 9 June in Australia, with Argentina winning 1–0.[36]

However, Argentina greatly struggled during the qualifiers, and it took a
[Lionel Messi](/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") hat trick at Ecuador to
confirm qualification for the [2018 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup
"2018 FIFA World Cup").[37] On 14 May 2018, Sampaoli announced a 35-man
preliminary squad for the 2018 World Cup.[38] He announced the final squad on
21 May 2018.[39]

At the World Cup, Argentina had drawn 1–1 with
[Iceland](/wiki/Iceland_national_football_team "Iceland national football
team") during their opening World Cup group match, an underwhelming
performance that drew criticism from former Argentine captain and coach [Diego
Maradona](/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona").[40] In the next group match,
Argentina suffered a heavy 0–3 loss by
[Croatia](/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football
team") due to "a defence left exposed, a midfield that was overrun and an
attack that was blunted", which put them on the brink of elimination and led
to unconfirmed reports that Sampaoli would be sacked.[41] Senior members of
the team including Messi and [Javier Mascherano](/wiki/Javier_Mascherano
"Javier Mascherano") confronted Sampaoli and his assistants in the dressing
room, while also approaching members of the Argentine FA to discuss their
concerns, and there were also various rumors that Messi was involved in team
selection which dismissed Sampaoli's leadership, evoking a formation based on
the decisions of Argentine players.[42] The match against Croatia was his 13th
game in charge, where he had used 13 lineups[43] and a total of 59
players,[44] and despite a myriad of attacking choices the defence was
poor.[45][46][47][48]

Sampaoli remained in his position,[49] as Argentina defeated Nigeria 2–1 in
the third group match to advance to the [knockout
stage](/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout
stage").[50] In the round of 16, Argentina lost to
[France](/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team")
4–3 and were eliminated from the tournament.[51]

On 15 July 2018, the Argentine Football Association announced that Sampaoli
had left his position as national coach by mutual consent.[52][53]

### Santos

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=14 "Edit
section: Santos")]

On 13 December 2018, Brazilian club [Santos](/wiki/Santos_FC "Santos FC")
announced that Sampaoli had reached an "agreement in principle" to become the
club's coach for the 2019 season.[54] He signed a two-year contract on 17
December,[55] being presented the following day.

Sampaoli was highly praised by the media during his time at the club,
specifically due to the offensive football displayed. Despite being knocked
out of the year's [Campeonato Paulista](/wiki/Campeonato_Paulista "Campeonato
Paulista") and [Copa Sudamericana](/wiki/Copa_Sudamericana "Copa
Sudamericana"), he took the club to the second position in the [Série
A](/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_S%C3%A9rie_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série
A").[56]

On 9 December 2019, Sampaoli resigned; Santos announced the departure of the
coach in the following day.[57]

### Atlético Mineiro

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=15 "Edit
section: Atlético Mineiro")]

On 1 March 2020, Sampaoli took charge of [Atlético
Mineiro](/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Mineiro "Clube Atlético Mineiro").[58] On
22 February 2021, Sampaoli requested the termination of his contract at the
end of the current season. On the same day, Atlético Mineiro announced that
they had accepted the termination of Sampaoli contract.[59]

### Marseille

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=16 "Edit
section: Marseille")]

On 26 February 2021, [Ligue 1](/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club
[Marseille](/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille") announced
Sampaoli as their coach until June 2023. He succeeded [Andre Villas-
Boas](/wiki/Andre_Villas-Boas "Andre Villas-Boas").[60]

### Return to Sevilla

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=17 "Edit
section: Return to Sevilla")]

On 6 October 2022, [Sevilla](/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") announced the
return of Sampaoli to be their coach.[61] On 21 March 2023, Sampaoli was
sacked after a 2–0 loss to [Getafe](/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF") left Sevilla
only two ponts above the relegation places; later that day, he was replaced by
[José Luis Mendilibar](/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Luis_Mendilibar "José Luis
Mendilibar").[62]

### Flamengo

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=18 "Edit
section: Flamengo")]

On 14 April 2023, Sampaoli returned to the [Campeonato Brasileiro Série
A](/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_S%C3%A9rie_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série A")
and [Copa Libertadores](/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") after
[Flamengo](/wiki/CR_Flamengo "CR Flamengo") announced that he signed a
contract as their coach until 31 December 2024.[63] On 28 September, he was
dismissed from his position.[64]

### Rennes

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=19 "Edit
section: Rennes")]

On 11 November 2024, he returned to [Ligue 1](/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") and was
appointed manager of [Rennes](/wiki/Stade_Rennais_F.C. "Stade Rennais F.C.")
on a contract until 2026.[65] On 30 January 2025, Sampaoli was sacked after a
series of bad results.[66]

### Return to Atlético Mineiro

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Jorge_Sampaoli&action=edit&section=20 "Edit
section: Return to Atlético Mineiro")]

On 2 September 2025, it was announced the return of Sampaoli to [Atlético
Mineiro](/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Mineiro "Clube Atlético Mineiro") on a
contract running until December 2027.[67]
